translation_notes: Every prov_graph.triples((None, p, o)) / .subjects(p, o) / .objects(s, p) / .value(s, p) becomes m{ }, one island per site, never merged -- e.g. len(list(prov_graph.triples((None, RDF.type, self.ONTOLOGY.Parameter)))) -> m{ ?s rdf:type {self.ONTOLOGY.Parameter} }.count(). REVISED from an earlier draft that kept `len(list(m{ }))` here: INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2 says to always use the MOST SPECIFIC construction and never degrade, and `.count()` is exactly that construction (listed alongside .first()/.one()/bool() as one of the four island reductions) -- keeping len(list(...)) under-credits it for no fidelity gain, since m{ }.count() and len(list(g.triples(pattern))) count the exact same multiset.

Each `(s, p, o) in prov_graph` membership test (self, ALPACA and self.ONTOLOGY terms only known at runtime) becomes bool(m{ {s} {p} {o} }), the trav_existence idiom -- used here even though the region was sampled for trav_one_step, per INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2's 'credit every island separately': the most specific construction at EACH site, not only the one the stratum sampled on.

list(m{ ?s a {X} })[0] (subjects filtered to a single match, confirmed by the preceding .count()==1 assertions) becomes m{ ?s a {X} }.first() -- the trav_single_value idiom, same 'most specific per site' reasoning as .count() above.

self.ONTOLOGY.X and ALPACA.X (both plain Python attribute access on runtime Namespace objects, not compile-time prefixes) interpolate as {self.ONTOLOGY.X} / {ALPACA.X} in every term position, subject and predicate included -- there is no @prefix for either in this file.

Literal('param_1') -> the bare Turtle string "param_1" (an untyped plain literal, matching Literal(str) exactly); Literal(45) -> the bare integer 45 (rdflib's Literal(int) constructor already infers datatype=xsd:integer, the same inference the language's own default coercion performs on a native Python int, so no explicit ^^xsd:integer is needed -- this is NOT the unsafe case INSTRUCTIONS_403 SS2bis warns about, which is an *explicit* datatype= on a non-string value).

prov_graph.value(attribute, ALPACA.pairName).toPython() -> m{ {attribute} {ALPACA.pairName} ?v }.first().toPython(): .value()'s None-when-missing and .first()'s None-when-missing agree, so calling .toPython() on either raises the same AttributeError when the pattern has no solution -- no special-casing needed for fidelity.

The region now genuinely executes end to end through alpaca's own real call-stack introspection, not a stand-in.

Context shim alpaca_context.py: EXAMPLE_NS, InputObject, OutputObject and the @Provenance-decorated process_multiple (plus its __ontology__ metadata assignment), reproduced verbatim from INM-6/alpaca@2b8dd34fc6f9a4c1ed2004e014b3ed9495eda1ba's alpaca/test/test_ontology_annotation.py (module scope, outside the extracted method's own lines 539-631) -- these are genuine test fixtures the upstream file itself defines, not invented logic. self.ONTOLOGY (bound by OntologyAnnotationTestCase.setUpClass) and the assert*/self plumbing are supplied by driver.py instead (a call argument, not a binding the shim should own), via a minimal real unittest.TestCase subclass -- see driver.py.

Second obstacle, found only after installing alpaca: its Provenance decorator reads the CALLING FRAME's source via inspect.getsourcelines()/linecache to build alpaca:codeStatement etc. (alpaca/code_analysis/source_code.py). The harness compiles translated.ldpy's TRANSPILED Python but tags the code object with the original .ldpy path (rdfeval/harness.py:_exec_ldpy, as it must -- that IS the region's file), so a naive linecache read finds the raw island syntax on disk and alpaca's own ast.parse() raises SyntaxError -- nothing to do with any rdflib triple. Fixed entirely within driver.py (no changes to rdfeval/ or ldpy/) by pre-populating linecache.cache for that path with the actual transpiled text before entry/calls run -- the standard technique doctest/IPython use for dynamically compiled code; it changes nothing about what executes, it only lets a third-party library's own introspection see it. This is a genuine, general characteristic of running source-introspecting Python code (frame-based, not just traceback-line, tooling) from a transpiled .ldpy file, worth a note for pilotage even though it does not block this particular region once worked around.
